arguments.command: tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Generating timing entropy" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\nResult: " && flips=""; while [ ${#flips} -lt 256 ]; do coin=0; t=$(date +%s%N); t=$((t + 1000000)); while [ $(date +%s%N) -lt $t ]; do coin=$((coin ^ 1)); done; flips="${flips}${coin}"; done; echo "$flips" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}' && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Generates a 256-bit entropy string using nanosecond clock drift loops compatible with Bash and Zsh, hashes it with sha256sum, and outputs the random string.
arguments.goal: Generate a secure random hash using timing drift entropy

arguments.command:

arguments.command:

" && qrencode -t UTF8 "$qrtext" && printf ""

arguments.command:
printf "1) 🎧 Listen for connection (Server)
2) 🔌 Connect to a colleague (Client)

" && read -rp "Choose (1-2): " choice && tput cuu 1 && if [ "$choice" = "1" ]; then read -rp "🔌 Port to open (default 4444): " port && port=${port:-4444} && tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Waiting for colleague connection" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "

"; fi && printf ""
